header.running_head: The Bravery of Our Guide Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.text: (moving speedily and fluidly. This happened by the blessings of Rasulullaah ﷺ)."[^1]

Another narration states that when an alarm was raised in Madinah, Rasulullaah ﷺ borrowed Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA)'s horse whose name was Mandoob. Rasulullaah ﷺ mounted the horse (and after investigating) he reassured the people saying, "We have seen nothing alarming but have found this horse to be like an ocean." Hadhrat Anas (RA) also said, "Whenever the battle grew furious, we always sought refuge with Rasulullaah ﷺ."[^2]
Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "During the Battle of Badr, we sought refuge from the Mushrikeen by the side of Rasulullaah ﷺ because he was the most furious of fighters."[^3]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Bravery During the Battle of Hunayn and the Statement of Hadhrat Baraa (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq reports that a man from the Qais tribe once asked Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA), "Did you people desert Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Hunayn?" Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq then heard Hadhrat Baraa (RA) reply, "However, Rasulullaah ﷺ did not desert. The Hawaazin tribe were ace archers. When we attacked them, they were defeated but when we occupied ourselves with collecting the booty, they intercepted us with a torrent of arrows. I then saw Rasulullaah ﷺ still on his white mule with Abu Sufyaan (RA) holding its reins. Rasulullaah ﷺ was saying, 'أَنَا النَّبِيُّ لَا كَذِبْ (I am a Nabi without a lie)'." Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said:
"أَنَا النَّبِيُّ لَا كَذِبْ. أَنَا ابْنُ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبْ"
"I am a Nabi without a lie. I am the son of Abdul Muttalib"
Yet another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ then dismounted the mule.[^4]

Hadhrat Baraa (RA) also narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ then descended from his mule and prayed for assistance saying:
"أَنَا النَّبِيُّ لَا كَذِبْ. أَنَا ابْنُ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبْ. اَللّٰهُمَّ نَزِّلْ نَصْرَكَ"
"I am a Nabi without a lie. I am the son of Abdul Muttalib. O Allaah! Send down Your assistance"
Hadhrat Baraa (RA) says further, "When the battle grew furious, we took refuge with Rasulullaah ﷺ and it was only the bravest ones who could fight by his side."[^5]

In the chapter concerning the bravery of the Sahabah (RA) in Jihaad, the incidents have already passed about the bravery of Hadhrat Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Talha, Zubayr, Sa'd, Hamzah, Abbaas, Mu'aadh, Ibn Umar, Mu'aadh bin Afraa, Abu
Ahmad and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.37).
Bukhaari. Muslim and Nasa'ee have reported a similar narration.
